rationale: The conditioner swap from stock leverage to near-term cash coverage is an economically distinct fragility channel and the sign logic is internally consistent, but the funding-gap leg is essentially the well-documented external-financing/free-cash-flow anomaly, so the incremental content rests entirely on whether the liquidity interaction survives controlling for the gap alone.

Both legs are identical to the archive's ExternalFinancingGapLeverage with only the accumulation window changed from one to three years — a cosmetic horizon variant rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the three-year sum of capex-minus-OCF is close to a rescaled version of cumulative asset/financing growth already known to predict returns.

The second-moment conditioner is a genuinely new channel in this archive and the sign is coherent, but earnings volatility is itself a documented standalone return predictor closely tied to idiosyncratic volatility and distress, so the test must show the product beats the volatility leg alone; a 5-year annual VOL will also thin coverage and lag badly.

The two legs are mechanically linked — growth in gross PP&E raises the denominator of sale/ppent and thus almost automatically produces a negative turnover delta — so the product is largely a nonlinear transform of capital/asset growth, which is a well-known published anomaly rather than a distinct capacity-utilization signal.

Replacing the intangible-collateral leg's leverage conditioner with cash coverage is a legitimate diagnosis-driven redesign rather than a cosmetic tweak, but COALESCE(gdwl,0) creates a large tied mass at zero so that for most firms the composite collapses to the cash-coverage leg alone, which should be reported as a diagnostic against the coverage-only benchmark.

This is the archive's ExternalFinancingGapLeverage with an industry z-score substituted for the raw leverage rank, and the switch to a signed conditioner silently changes the economics — high-deficit, below-industry-leverage firms are now pushed to the long leg, an implication the hypothesis never argues for and which contradicts the stated "penalize abnormal indebtedness" framing.
